title: Planar random clusters, sharpness and the exact square-lattice critical point

items.title: Finite FK random-cluster weights for real q and boundary partitions
items.statement:
Let $G=(V,E,\partial)$ be a finite undirected multigraph: $V$ and the edge-label set $E$ are finite, and each $e\in E$ has a singleton or two-element endpoint set $\partial e\subseteq V$. Distinct labels may have the same endpoint set. Let $B\subseteq V$ be a designated boundary set and let $\xi$ be an equivalence relation on $B$; vertices in each $\xi$-class are wired together, while vertices outside $B$ remain separate. For $A\subseteq E$, let $k_\xi(A)$ be the number of connected components, including isolated vertices, after wiring the $\xi$-classes and opening exactly the edges in $A$. A loop does not join distinct vertices.

For $q\in[1,\infty)$ and $p\in(0,1)$, the finite FK weight of $A$ and its partition function are

$$w_{G,p,q}^{\xi}(A):=p^{|A|}(1-p)^{|E\setminus A|}q^{k_\xi(A)},\qquad Z_{G,p,q}^{\xi}:=\sum_{A\subseteq E}w_{G,p,q}^{\xi}(A).$$

The finite FK random-cluster probability is $\phi_{G,p,q}^{\xi}(A):=w_{G,p,q}^{\xi}(A)/Z_{G,p,q}^{\xi}$. Every weight is positive and finite, and the finite sum $Z_{G,p,q}^{\xi}$ is positive and finite. The free boundary condition is the identity partition on $B$; the wired boundary condition identifies all vertices of $B$ in one class.

When $G$ is a finite simple graph with the Potts/FK convention of the earlier finite Potts definition, $\xi$ is free, $q=Q$ is an integer at least two, and every activity equals $v=p/(1-p)$, this definition gives the same normalized FK law, since $w_{FK}(A)=(1-p)^{-|E|}w_{G,p,Q}^{\xi}(A)$.

items.title: Free, wired, and subsequential infinite-volume FK states on the square lattice
items.statement:
Let $E_\infty$ be the nearest-neighbor edge set of $\mathbb Z^2$, and let $\Lambda_n=[-n,n]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. Let $E_n$ contain the edges with both endpoints in $\Lambda_n$, and let $\partial\Lambda_n$ be the vertices of $\Lambda_n$ adjacent to a vertex outside it. Fix $q\geq1$ and $p\in(0,1)$. For each boundary partition $\xi_n$ on $\partial\Lambda_n$, let $\phi_{n,p,q}^{\xi_n}$ be the finite FK law of [[def-csm-frontier-fk-real-boundaries]] on $(\Lambda_n,E_n)$ and extend its configurations to $\{0,1\}^{E_\infty}$ by setting all edges outside $E_n$ closed.

An **infinite-volume FK state** at $(p,q)$ is any probability measure on $\{0,1\}^{E_\infty}$ that is a cylinder-probability limit of such extended finite-volume laws along a sequence $n_j\to\infty$ and boundary partitions $\xi_{n_j}$. Cylinder-probability convergence means convergence of the probability of every assignment on every finite set of edges. When they exist, the **free FK state** and **wired FK state** are the cylinder limits for the identity and one-class partitions, respectively, at every $n$. Their existence and uniqueness as cylinder limits are established by a later A-page lemma. For either state $\phi^b_{p,q}$, $b\in\{0,1\}$, define $\theta^b(p,q):=\phi^b_{p,q}(0\leftrightarrow\infty)$, where $0\leftrightarrow\infty$ means that the open cluster of the origin is not contained in any finite box, and define

$$p_c^b(q):=\inf\{p\in(0,1):\theta^b(p,q)>0\}.$$

No equality of free and wired states at $p=p_c$ is part of this definition.

items.title: Finite FK association, spatial Markov property, and boundary monotonicity
items.statement:
For every finite undirected multigraph $G=(V,E,\partial)$, boundary set $B\subseteq V$, boundary partition $\xi$ on $B$, $q\geq1$, and $p\in(0,1)$, the finite FK law defined by the stated finite weights is strictly positive and log-supermodular on the Boolean lattice $2^E$: for $A,C\subseteq E$,

$$\phi_{G,p,q}^{\xi}(A\cup C)\phi_{G,p,q}^{\xi}(A\cap C)\geq\phi_{G,p,q}^{\xi}(A)\phi_{G,p,q}^{\xi}(C).$$

Consequently it is positively associated: $\phi(fg)\geq\phi(f)\phi(g)$ for increasing real functions $f,g:2^E\to\mathbb R$. Conditioning on the states of all edges outside a finite edge set $F$ gives a finite FK law on $F$ whose boundary partition wires exactly the vertices joined by the fixed exterior open edges and the original partition $\xi$. Given all other edge states, an edge is open with conditional probability $p$ if its endpoints are already connected, and $p/(p+q(1-p))$ otherwise. If $p_1\leq p_2$ and $\xi_1$ refines $\xi_2$ (each $\xi_1$-class lies in a $\xi_2$-class), then $\phi_{p_1,q}^{\xi_1}\leq_{st}\phi_{p_2,q}^{\xi_2}$.

items.title: Planar FK duality with the free exterior-face convention
items.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected plane graph with a fixed embedding and $|V|\geq1$. Use the free partition on all primal vertices, $B=V$. Its plane dual multigraph $G^*$ has one vertex for each face, including the unbounded face, and one dual edge $e^*$ crossing each primal edge $e$; use the identity partition on the dual face-vertices. The unbounded face is one dual vertex, so this convention retains the exterior-face connection in the dual. For a primal open set $A\subseteq E$, let $A^*:=\{e^*:e\in E\setminus A\}$, so a dual edge is open exactly when its crossing primal edge is closed. For $q\geq1$ and $p\in(0,1)$ define $p^*\in(0,1)$ by

$$\frac{p^*}{1-p^*}=q\frac{1-p}{p}.$$

Then complementing the primal edges sends the finite FK law $\phi_{G,p,q}^{\mathrm{free}}$ to the dual FK law $\phi_{G^*,p^*,q}^{\mathrm{free}}$: the random dual edge set $A^*$ has exactly that distribution. The unnormalized weight ratio is the configuration-independent factor $q^{|V|-1}((1-p)/p^*)^{|E|}$; the exponent $|V|-1$ includes the exterior-face contribution under this identity-partition convention.

items.title: Existence of the free and wired infinite-volume FK limits
items.statement: For every $q\geq1$ and $p\in(0,1)$, the free finite-volume FK laws on $\Lambda_n$ are stochastically increasing under restriction as $n$ grows, and the wired finite-volume FK laws are stochastically decreasing under restriction. Both sequences therefore have unique cylinder-probability limits, and those limits are probability measures on $\{0,1\}^{E_\infty}$; hence the free and wired infinite-volume states are well-defined.

references.locator: Chapter 4, finite-volume free/wired limits and stochastic boundary comparison.

items.title: Opposite crossings of a rectangular grid intersect
items.statement: Let $a,b\geq1$ be integers and let $Q_{a,b}=\{0,\ldots,a\}\times\{0,\ldots,b\}$ have its nearest-neighbor square-grid edges, drawn as unit horizontal and vertical segments. A left-to-right path is a finite edge path whose endpoints lie on the sides $x=0$ and $x=a$; a bottom-to-top path is defined analogously using $y=0$ and $y=b$. Every left-to-right path and every bottom-to-top path in $Q_{a,b}$ share a vertex.

items.title: Periodic-torus RSW lower bounds at the FK self-dual point
items.statement: For each $q\geq1$ and aspect ratio $\alpha>1$, there is a constant $c(\alpha,q)>0$ such that the following holds. Let $n,m$ be positive integers with $m>\lceil\alpha n\rceil$, let $T_m=(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^2$ with its nearest-neighbor horizontal and vertical edges and periodic boundary conditions, and give its edges the FK law with no boundary wiring, parameter $q$, and $p_{\rm sd}(q)=\sqrt q/(1+\sqrt q)$. The probability of a horizontal open crossing of the vertex rectangle $\{0,\ldots,\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor\}\times\{0,\ldots,n\}$ is at least $c(\alpha,q)$, uniformly in $n$ and $m$.

items.title: A maximum conditional edge influence bound for finite FK measures
items.statement:
Let $G=(V,E,\partial)$ be a finite undirected multigraph, let $B\subseteq V$ have boundary partition $\xi$, fix $q\geq1$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$, and $p\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$, and let $\phi=\phi_{G,p,q}^{\xi}$ be the finite FK law. For every increasing event $A\subseteq2^E$ with $0<\phi(A)<1$ and $|E|\geq2$, define the conditional influence of edge $e$ by

$$I_A(e):=\phi(A\mid \omega_e=1)-\phi(A\mid\omega_e=0).$$

There is a constant $c(q,\varepsilon)>0$ such that

$$\max_{e\in E}I_A(e)\geq c(q,\varepsilon)\,\phi(A)(1-\phi(A))\frac{\log|E|}{|E|}.$$

items.title: Crossing sharpness and subcritical decay for square-lattice FK
items.statement:
Put $p_{\rm sd}(q)=\sqrt q/(1+\sqrt q)$. Assume the periodic-torus crossing estimates at $p_{\rm sd}(q)$ from [[thm-csm-frontier-fk-torus-rsw]], the influence inequality from [[lem-csm-frontier-fk-influence-threshold]], and the following two unresolved inputs. First, the source's wired-boundary path construction must convert the polynomial high-probability torus crossing estimates into $\theta^1(p,q)>0$ for every $p>p_{\rm sd}(q)$. Second, its subcritical finite-size/Hamming-distance argument, including the greedy-lattice-animal bound, must give constants $C,c>0$ such that $\phi^1_{p,q}(x\leftrightarrow y)\leq C e^{-c\lVert x-y\rVert_2}$ for $p<p_{\rm sd}(q)$. Under these hypotheses, both conclusions hold. In particular, $p_c^1(q)=p_{\rm sd}(q)$, where $p_c^1$ is defined in [[def-csm-frontier-fk-infinite-volume-states]].

The same hypotheses imply the identical free threshold if, in addition, the planar free/wired threshold-coincidence input recorded below is supplied. They do not assert equality of the free and wired measures at $p=p_{\rm sd}(q)$.

items.title: Exact square-lattice FK critical point and subcritical decay
items.statement:
For every real $q\geq1$, put $p_{\rm sd}(q)=\sqrt q/(1+\sqrt q)$. For every $p>p_{\rm sd}(q)$, the wired state has $\theta^1(p,q)>0$; for every $p<p_{\rm sd}(q)$, both free and wired states have zero percolation probability and the free and wired critical thresholds defined in [[def-csm-frontier-fk-infinite-volume-states]] equal $p_{\rm sd}(q)$. For every $p<p_{\rm sd}(q)$, there are constants $C(p,q),c(p,q)>0$ such that every cylinder-limit FK state $\phi$ on $\mathbb Z^2$ satisfies
$$\phi(x\leftrightarrow y)\leq C(p,q)e^{-c(p,q)\lVert x-y\rVert_2}\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb Z^2).$$
No equality of the free and wired measures at $p=p_{\rm sd}(q)$, critical exponent, or order of transition is asserted.

items.title: Square-lattice Potts critical inverse temperature
items.statement:
Let $Q\geq2$ be an integer, $J>0$, and $\beta>0$. On $\Lambda_n=[-n,n]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, let $B_n=\{x\in\Lambda_n:\lVert x\rVert_\infty=n\}$ and let $E_n$ be the nearest-neighbor edges with both endpoints in $\Lambda_n$. The $Q$-state Potts model has spins $\sigma:\Lambda_n\to\{1,\ldots,Q\}$, fixed plus boundary $\sigma|_{B_n}=1$, and finite-volume Gibbs probabilities proportional to $e^{-\beta H_n(\sigma)}$, where
$$H_n(\sigma)=-J\sum_{\{x,y\}\in E_n}\mathbf1_{\{\sigma_x=\sigma_y\}}.$$
Define its plus-boundary order parameter by
$$m_Q^+(\beta):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P_{\beta,n}^+(\sigma_0=1)-Q^{-1},$$
when the limit exists, and define $\beta_c:=\inf\{\beta>0:m_Q^+(\beta)>0\}$. Then the limit exists and
$$\beta_c J=\log(1+\sqrt Q).$$
The assertion is conditional on the FK exact-threshold input in [[thm-csm-frontier-fk-square-critical-point]] and the current finite Potts/FK interfaces identified below.

references.title: Vincent Beffara and Hugo Duminil-Copin, The self-dual point of the two-dimensional random-cluster model is critical for q >= 1
references.locator: Theorem 3 and Section 1: finite Potts/FK coupling and the square-lattice critical-temperature formula.

references.title: Geoffrey Grimmett, The Random-Cluster Model, second edition
references.locator: Chapter 1 §§1.2–1.4, finite Potts/FK coupling, and Chapter 6, square-lattice critical point.

items.title: Square-lattice Ising critical coupling from the two-state Potts model
items.statement:
On $\Lambda_n=[-n,n]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, let $E_n$ be the nearest-neighbor edges with both endpoints in $\Lambda_n$ and fix plus boundary spins $\sigma_x=+1$ whenever $\lVert x\rVert_\infty=n$. For $\sigma_x\in\{-1,+1\}$, define the finite-volume Ising Hamiltonian and Gibbs law by
$$H_{I,n}(\sigma)=-J_I\sum_{\{x,y\}\in E_n}\sigma_x\sigma_y,\qquad \mathbb P_{\beta,n}^{I,+}(\sigma)\propto e^{-\beta H_{I,n}(\sigma)},\quad J_I>0.$$
Define $m_I^+(\beta):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P_{\beta,n}^{I,+}(\sigma_0=+1)-1/2$ when the limit exists, and $\beta_c^I:=\inf\{\beta>0:m_I^+(\beta)>0\}$. The limit exists and
$$\beta_c^I J_I=\tfrac12\log(1+\sqrt2).$$

references.title: Vincent Beffara and Hugo Duminil-Copin, The self-dual point of the two-dimensional random-cluster model is critical for q >= 1
references.locator: Theorem 3, q=2 Potts critical inverse temperature.
